head: Five seconds.
Then it
pulls the plug.
body: Our service crashed for thousands of users, and the stack trace blamed a line that does nothing wrong.
It only happened on cheap phones. That was the clue.

head: It runs the
*night shift
slides.caption: It gives you about five seconds to explain why your work belongs, then closes the cell. Not cruel. Just running the prison by the book.

head: Five seconds spent
before the promise
callout: On a cold, loaded phone those two reads blow past the window, and the system kills the service before you ever keep the promise.

head: Two disk reads,
one dead service
slides.caption: The countdown starts the moment you call startForegroundService(). On a cold, loaded phone those reads spend the whole window.

items.title: startForeground() first
items.sub: before any init, permission read or coroutine

items.title: Then do the slow work
items.sub: warm-up, GPS, network, all of it after

items.title: Cheap devices are the truth
items.sub: a cold, loaded phone is your real deadline

head: The platform is
not out to get you
body: It is protecting the user's battery and attention from apps that want to run forever.
Post your notification first, work with the lifecycle, and it leaves you alone.
